title: More than 100,000 ethnic Armenians flee Nagorno-Karabakh to Armenia
body:
By Sunday, 1 October 2023, well over 100,000 ethnic Armenians from Nagorno-Karabakh had travelled to Armenia, according to the World Health Organization. Nazeli Baghdasaryan, spokeswoman for the Armenian prime minister, said that 100,490 forcefully displaced persons had arrived in Armenia by that morning. Nearly all of Karabakh's estimated 120,000 residents left in the days following Azerbaijan's offensive of 19 and 20 September. The WHO figure and the Armenian government figure were consistent with one another, both exceeding 100,000 against a pre-offensive population estimated at 120,000.

The same day a United Nations mission arrived in Nagorno-Karabakh, the first UN access to the region in about 30 years. An Azerbaijani presidency spokesman said the mission, led by a senior UN aid official, had come mainly to assess humanitarian needs. Al Jazeera's Osama Bin Javaid, reporting from Stepanakert, which Azerbaijanis call Khankendi, described a mass exodus and said almost no one remained in the town centre apart from some disabled and elderly people.
